questions.question: What are the six pillars of a comprehensive AI usage policy?
choices: Budget, timeline, team size, tools, vendor, support
Approved tools, prohibited uses, data handling, attribution, consequences, review cadence
Security, performance, reliability, cost, compliance, monitoring
Planning, development, testing, deployment, monitoring, retirement
questions.explanation: A complete AI usage policy must cover: approved tools & permitted uses, prohibited uses, data handling rules, attribution & disclosure, consequences for violations, and review/update cadence.

questions.question: Why is 'use AI tools responsibly' an ineffective policy statement?
choices: It's too short to fit in a document
It's too vague to be enforced — specific prohibitions are needed
It doesn't mention which AI tools to use
It only applies to senior developers
questions.explanation: Vague policies are unenforceable. A good policy names specific tools, lists specific prohibitions (like 'don't paste customer PII into AI tools'), and defines specific consequences.

questions.question: Why must an AI usage policy have a review cadence?
choices: Legal requirements mandate monthly policy reviews
AI tools change rapidly — a policy from 2024 may reference tools that no longer exist
Review cadences make policies look more professional
It's a way to give the compliance team more work
questions.explanation: AI tools and their data practices evolve quickly. A policy that isn't reviewed quarterly may reference deprecated tools, miss new risks, or fail to address newly discovered vulnerabilities.
